An object V together with an arrow going from V to each object of a diagram such that for any arrow A in the diagram, the pair of arrows from V which subtend A also commute with it. (Then V can be said to be the cone’s vertex and the diagram which the cone subtends can be said to be its base.)

examples.text: A cone is an object (the apex) and a natural transformation from a constant functor (whose image is the apex of the cone and its identity morphism) to a diagram functor. Its components are projections from the apex to the objects of the diagram and it has a “naturality triangle” for each morphism in the diagram. (A “naturality triangle” is just a naturality square which is degenerate at its apex side.)

Organe reproducteur chez la plupart des gymnospermes, en particulier chez les conifères, formé d’un axe central portant des écailles disposées en spirale. Le cône mâle, généralement petit, tendre et caduc, produit le pollen, tandis que le cône femelle, persistant, porte des ovules qui, après la fécondation, se transforment en graines et se lignifie pour les protéger jusqu’à leur dispersion. Ce type de structure est aussi appelé strobile.
